chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Keep the Ra'abiyyah pigeons in your houses, for they curse the killers of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and may Allah curse his killer.

key_terms.الرَّاعِبِيَّةَ: A specific breed or type of pigeons mentioned in this narration.
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ: Husayn ibn Ali, the third Shia Imam.
key_terms.تَلْعَنُ: They curse (verb form indicating continuous or characteristic action).
key_terms.قَتَلَةَ: The killers or slayers (plural of qatil).

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of keeping Ra'abiyyah pigeons in the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recommends keeping the 'Ra'abiyyah' breed of pigeons in homes as a tangible symbol of devotion, noting that they curse the killers of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him). This practice underscores the Shia tradition of 'Tajalli al-Awliya' (manifestation of the saints) in creation, where natural entities reflect spiritual realities and honor the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a daily, domestic reminder of the tragedy of Karbala and the enduring curse upon its perpetrators.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Take Al-Ra’aiby pigeons to be in your houses, for these curse the killers of Al-Husaynasws Bin Aliasws, and Allahazwj Curses hisasws killers’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must keep al-Ra’‘ibiy pigeon in your homes because it condemns the murderers of al-Husayn ibn Ali, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and Allah has condemned his killer.’”
